narrative: Window is 23 to 29 September against 16 to 22 September. 23 September is still missing from the source data, so the current window holds 6 real days against 7, and per day figures are the fairer read. Totals look flat (spend ₹10,248 vs ₹10,910, leads 194 vs 195), but per day spend rose 9.6% (₹1,708 vs ₹1,558) and leads rose 16% (32.3 vs 27.9). Cost per lead improved 5.6% to ₹52.82 (from ₹55.95), so the extra budget is converting slightly better, not worse.

CPM rose 18.1% to ₹81.04 (from ₹68.59) while CTR edged up to 1.16% (from 1.05%) and hook rate held near 27%. The strong stretch continued: 25 to 28 September delivered 35, 44, 35 and 34 leads, and 29 September still produced a healthy day. Pricing pressure is the one trend that keeps building, but higher CTR is absorbing it.

Budget kept rotating away from the dominant ad: 'VP_Animated-Static_17July26' fell to ₹4,781 (from ₹7,718) at 0.81% CTR. 'VP| Vastu video|NewContent|07Jul26 – Copy' rose to ₹1,543 (from ₹214) at 1.32% CTR, and 'VP_Vastu-Shanti_17July26' grew to ₹544 (from ₹41) with CTR up to 2.54%, the best in the account. The new 'VP_Animated-Static_28Sept26' started with ₹617 of spend at 0.84% CTR.

callout.title: Leads up 16% per day and CPL down, but CPM is up 18%
callout.body: Per day leads rose from 27.9 to 32.3 while CPL fell to ₹52.82. CPM has now climbed for a third straight pull (₹68.59 to ₹81.04 this time). Volume and CTR are absorbing it for now, but a dip in lead flow would push CPL up quickly.

actions: Give 'VP_Vastu-Shanti_17July26' a larger test budget. It has the best CTR in the account (2.54%) and only ₹544 of spend.
'VP| Vastu video|NewContent|07Jul26 – Copy' is scaling at 1.32% CTR. Keep letting it take share from the static and watch for fatigue.
'VP_Animated-Static_28Sept26' is at 0.84% CTR, in line with the older static it resembles. Give it two or three more days before deciding whether it earns budget.
Watch CPM against CPL daily. If CPL crosses ₹60 with CPM still rising, refresh creative before adding budget.

narrative: Window is 23 to 29 September against 16 to 22 September, with 23 September missing so the current window has 6 real days. Spend per day held steady (₹1,638 vs ₹1,583, +3.5%) but chats fell hard: 49.7 a day against 71.6 (down 31%). Cost per chat rose 49% to ₹32.98 (from ₹22.12). This is a clear step down and the biggest negative movement across the account this pull.

CTR dropped to 1.37% (from 2.59%) while hook rate rose to 18.5% (from 10.4%), meaning people are stopping on the ads but fewer click through to WhatsApp. The daily chat count tells the story: 16 to 22 September included days of 83, 74 and 123 chats, while every day in this window sat between 35 and 62.

The cause is visible in the ad mix. 'VP_Baby-Shower_CarouselAD_17Aug26' (CTR 2.65%, down from 3.66%) had its spend halved to ₹3,261 from ₹6,306, and 'VP_Garbhsanskar_Customer_Testimonial_VideoAD_21-03-26' jumped to ₹3,238 from ₹580 at only 0.53% CTR. Budget moved from the strongest clicking ad to a weak one. The carousel itself is also showing early fatigue.

callout.title: Cost per chat up 49% as spend shifted to a 0.53% CTR video
callout.body: The testimonial video took roughly ₹2,650 of extra spend at 0.53% CTR while the carousel (2.65% CTR) lost ₹3,045. Chats per day fell from 71.6 to 49.7. Restoring the carousel's share, or refreshing it, is the first fix to try.

actions: Cap or pause 'VP_Garbhsanskar_Customer_Testimonial_VideoAD_21-03-26' and push budget back to 'VP_Baby-Shower_CarouselAD_17Aug26'.
Prepare a fresh variation of the baby shower carousel, since its CTR is slipping from 3.66% to 2.65%.
Check whether WhatsApp response time or the landing message changed, as hook rate rose while clicks fell.
Review again in two days. If cost per chat stays above ₹30, consider rebalancing the two ad sets.

narrative: Still a small sample (about ₹85 a day), so read gently. Window is 23 to 29 September against 16 to 22 September (23 September missing). Spend was ₹521 against ₹597, chats 20 against 21, and cost per chat improved 8% to ₹26.04 (from ₹28.43). Per day chats were 3.3 against 3.0.
CPM rose 49% to ₹43.88 (from ₹29.50) but CTR improved to 0.52% (from 0.41%) and frequency eased to 1.10. 29 September was the best day yet, with 8 chats on ₹183 of spend.
'VP_AppDownload_Static-1' still carries most of the spend (₹453) at 0.48% CTR, while 'VP_AppDownload_Video1' is small (₹68) but has a much higher CTR of 1.31%.

callout.title: Small sample: CPL is steady, video looks promising
callout.body: With only 20 chats in the window, day to day swings are noise. The one signal worth testing is the video ad's 1.31% CTR against 0.48% for the static, which rests on only ₹68 of spend.

actions: Raise the budget share of 'VP_AppDownload_Video1' modestly to test whether its 1.31% CTR holds at scale.
Track actual app installs from these chats, not only chat counts, before judging efficiency.
Hold the ad set budget steady until there are at least 50 chats in a window.
Watch CPM (up 49%) but do not act until it persists another pull.

narrative: Window is 23 to 29 September against 16 to 22 September, with 23 September missing so the current window has 6 days. ROAS fell to 1.60x from 2.03x. Per day spend dropped 13% (₹1,852 vs ₹2,131), but per day revenue dropped 31% (₹2,967 vs ₹4,324) and orders fell to 1.5 a day from 2.3. Shopify shows 9 orders and ₹17,805 revenue against 16 orders and ₹30,269. Meta shows 10 purchases against 17, so both sources agree on the decline and this is not attribution lag.

Two days with zero orders hurt: 21 September earlier and now 29 September, when ₹1,493 was spent with no sale. Hook rate fell sharply to 3.16% (from 8.77%) while CTR held at 2.48%, meaning the opening seconds of the video are no longer stopping people even though clickers still come.

Creative mix changed a lot. 'VP_Umbartha_NewVedio_copy' (3.43% CTR, the best clicker) dropped to ₹1,200 from ₹4,464, while the new 'VP_Umbartha Static_22Sept26' rose to ₹3,489 from ₹918 at 2.54% CTR. The catalog ad 'Umbartha_Catalog ads _18Sept26' and the L30 website engaged ad set both stopped (₹1,271 and about ₹1,195 of earlier spend now at zero).

callout.title: ROAS down to 1.60x, confirmed by both Meta and Shopify
callout.body: Orders fell from 16 to 9 and revenue from ₹30,269 to ₹17,805, with Meta and Shopify in agreement, so this is a real decline. The best CTR video lost most of its budget while a new static took over, and the retargeting audience (L30 engaged) has stopped spending.

actions: Return budget to 'VP_Umbartha_NewVedio_copy', which has the best CTR (3.43%) but only ₹1,200 of spend.
Judge 'VP_Umbartha Static_22Sept26' on orders, not CTR, since it now holds ₹3,489 of spend.
Re-enable a retargeting set (L30 website engaged), since it stopped and orders fell at the same time.
Refresh the video opening seconds, as hook rate fell to 3.16%.

narrative: Window is 23 to 29 September against 16 to 22 September, with 23 September missing so the current window has 6 days. This tab held steady with mild per day growth. callout.title: Steady 2.83x ROAS, with Meta undercounting purchases
callout.body: Meta reports 37 purchases while Shopify recorded 44 orders in the same window, so use Shopify as the source of truth. The rotation from static to video did not hurt ROAS.

actions: Test more budget on 'Numerology_Static_8Sept26' (1.85% CTR, only ₹835 spend).
Keep 'VP_Kundali-Namkaran_VideoAD_26Jun26' scaling while ROAS holds near 2.8x.
Watch 'VP_Baby_Kundali_Static_10sept26', which lost more than half its spend, for any further decline.
